node.title: Re: Mojo::DOM help
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
You're using Perl's or, which is taking the logical combination of those three strings before calling the find method, and since the first string is a true value, the only thing you're passing to the find method is the first string. See [mod://Mojo::DOM::CSS]'s selectors: "or" is a comma, and "and" for attributes is [...][...]. But note that class gets special treatment, and you can simply use the .class selector to match classes, stringing them together for an "and". Also note the order of classes in the class attribute can change, which the following shows, but if you really want exact string matches you can use the [class="value"] selectors.

use warnings; use 5.012; use Mojo::DOM; my $dom = Mojo::DOM->new(<<'HTML');
matches
no match
matches
matches
matches
matches
no match
matches
matches
no match
HTML $dom->find('.LC20lb.DKV0Md, .BNeawe.vvjwJb.AP7Wnd, .CVA68e.qXLe6d') ->each(sub { say });
